FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Monroe Canyon Burn Scar in...
South Central Sevier County in central Utah...

* Until 600 PM MDT.

* At 303 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Monroe Canyon Burn Scar. Between 0.5 and 0.75
inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow
moving through Monroe Canyon. The debris flow can consist of rock,
mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding in and around the Monroe
Canyon Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around
the Monroe Canyon Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Monroe.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and
ditches in the Monroe Canyon Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also
be anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away
in places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, roads and normally dry washes is likely. The heavy rains
will likely trigger rockslides, mudslides and debris flows in steep
terrain, especially in and around these areas.
